Subject: Post-call: Reliability & graceful degradation — recap + next steps

Hi Samantha / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have clear next steps. Please skim and flag anything I got wrong.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Production reliability: two customer-facing incidents in the last 3 months with failovers that required manual intervention.
- Latency tail: p99 spikes during peak (batch scoring) causing UI timeouts and unhappy customers.
- Lack of graceful degradation: no automated fallback to smaller/quantized models or cross-region routing.
- Observability gaps: limited token-level tracing and retention for audit/compliance.

Current stack you described:
- In-house model endpoints running on GCP Kubernetes (CPU + small GPU for bursts)
- Redis for session state; no KV cache optimized for decoder-only LLMs
- Custom autoscaler based on CPU, not request-rate/latency
- Audit logs exported to S3 but short retention for debug traces

Success criteria (what Finlytics would consider a win):
1) Reduce visible customer-facing incidents related to inference failures to <0.1% monthly.
2) End-to-end p99 latency for interactive flows reduced to <= 350ms under typical peak.
3) Automatic graceful degradation: fallback to smaller quantized model or cached responses when latency/SLOs are at risk.
4) Comprehensive audit logs + 90-day retention for traceability.

Initial reliability & graceful degradation options we discussed (how Redwood can help):
- Smart routing across regions and model variants to avoid single-region failures.
- Prefix/KV caching to eliminate repeat token work for common queries.
- Configurable fallback chains (e.g., full model -> quantized model -> canned response) with programmable triggers.
- Per-route SLOs and alerting; token-level cost/latency breakdowns for billing/debug.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20250722.pdf (brief notes + rough cost model) attached.

Next steps
- Action: Schedule 60-min technical deep dive with Aditya (SE) to go over incident telemetry and runbook integration — proposed slots below.
- Action: Samantha to share latency histograms and incident post-mortems (redacted as needed) — we can use these for a targeted pilot.
- Action: Redwoods to share SOC2 summary + fallback playbook (Aditya will send).

Proposed deep-dive times (PDT): Wed 7/23 10:00–11:00, Thu 7/24 09:00–10:00, Thu 7/24 16:00–17:00. Reply with preferred slot and we’ll calendar.

Thanks —

Thanks Samantha — great context. A few technical notes ahead of the deep dive so we can make the session actionable: 

On cross-region warm pools / fast failover:
- We support configurable warm pools in additional regions; warm pool sizing can be set as a % of baseline capacity. For pilot use we typically recommend 3–5% reserved for failover to reduce cold-start risk.
- Smart routing keeps sticky requests pinned when possible but will failover transparently to an alternate region if health checks fail. Failover is orthogonal to data residency — we can restrict to regions as needed.

On graceful degradation strategies:
- Model variant chain: full precision -> int8/quantized -> distilled model -> canned/cached answer. Triggers are configurable (latency threshold, error rate, queue length).
- Progressive response trimming: reduce max tokens and prioritize system prompts to preserve core facts.
- Cache-first routing for high-frequency queries (prefix/KV cache) to avoid repeated decoding work.

SLOs & observability:
- We expose per-route p50/p95/p99 latency and per-token cost. SLO alerting and mitigation policies can be tied to automated fallbacks.
- Audit logs (token-level traces) can be exported to your S3/GCS with configurable retention; default pilot retention is 90 days.

Pilot / pricing notes (very rough):
- Hosted fallback + smart-routing pilot (no reserved hardware): minimal setup fee + usage-based billing; good for proving reliability improvements quickly.
- Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit): higher baseline cost, predictable throughput and lower tail latency; we can size a pilot 1–3 weeks to validate improvements.

I attached our internal fallback playbook so you have a concrete reference before the deep dive (redwood-fallback-playbook.pdf). For the deep dive please bring:
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) bucketed by endpoint and time of day.
- Post-mortem notes you’re comfortable sharing (redacted).
- A small sample of logs showing the error patterns if possible.

Looking forward to Wed 7/23 10:00. I’ll include a calendar invite with a Zoom link and a brief agenda (1) incident walkthrough, (2) telemetry review, (3) proposed fallback configuration, (4) pilot next steps.
